title: HaloInsight POC - Cost Efficiency & Throughput Check-in
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on current pilot economics: tokens/sec/$, caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed last week's benchmark results, identified KV/prefix cache misconfiguration that inflated token costs, agreed to update batching policy and run a 24hr throughput window. Action: SE to re-run quantized model benchmark; AE to share updated pricing calc and short deck for execs.
next_steps: Owen to re-run 8-bit quantized throughput sweep and share CSV by 2025-10-04
Maya to send updated token-cost model and one-page exec summary by 2025-10-03
Ravi to enable prefix cache policy on dev cluster and report initial hit-rate by 2025-10-05
action_items: Owen Park: re-run quantized model benchmark (8-bit and 4-bit) and upload raw logs; due 2025-10-04
Maya Chen: update slide with tokens/sec/$ calc and add caching assumptions; due 2025-10-03
Ravi Patel: enable prefix/KV cache config on pilot dev; capture hit-rate and latency impact; due 2025-10-05

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood SE), Emma Gallagher (HaloInsight PM), Ravi Patel (HaloInsight Infra), Jules Moreno (HaloInsight ML), Samira N'Diaye (HaloInsight Head of Product)

[00:00] Maya (AE): okay, thanks everyone for hopping on, we'll do a quick econ check-in and then go into the throughput numbers. I see Samira and Emma joined, great — quick context, last week we saw higher tokens per dollar than expected on the hosted run.
[00:18] Emma (PM): yeah we were surprised; our stake holders are asking why the cost jumped when we turned on the longer context tests.
[00:26] Owen (SE): short answer is likely caching and batching interplay. We had prefix cache mis-hit rates and a conservative batching policy set by default. So the per-token CPU / GPU time increased, which amplified tokens/$ numbers.
[00:39] Ravi (Infra): can you clarify mis-hit? we thought we had prefix caching enabled in the pilot config.
[00:45] Owen (SE): you did, but the policy was set to 'prefix_cache: off_first_token' for the long-doc path. That maker a lot of repeated KV loads. The analytics show hit-rate around 18% on the long-doc workload, expected 60-70%.
[01:00] Maya (AE): to ground folks, last week's headline: we measured about 1,200 tokens/sec per $ on the short-chat workload but only ~420 tokens/sec per $ on the long-doc traces. We're trying to get those numbers closer by tuning cache and batching.
[01:18] Jules (ML): do you have the raw numbers for latency P95? tail matters for our product.
[01:24] Owen (SE): yes, short-chat P95 was 120ms while long-doc P95 spiked to 740ms under the same qps. Tail correlates with reloading KV cache and smaller batching sizes.
[01:36] Samira (Head Product): what's the tradeoff if we push batching higher? Sounds like we save cost but could hurt latency.
[01:44] Owen (SE): exactly. Increasing batch window from 12ms to 40ms improved tokens/sec/$ by about 28% in our test, but P95 increased by ~90ms for the short-chat path. For the long-doc workload, batching helps more because there's more shared prefixes to amortize the KV loads.
[02:00] Emma (PM): can we do adaptive batching? like latency SLA for chat endpoints but aggressive batching for document summarization?
[02:06] Maya (AE): yes, that's part of Redwood Optimize suggestions — per-route batching profiles. We can set policy: max_latency_sla and target_cost. Owen, any notes on setting that up?
[02:14] Owen (SE): yep, we can create a canary rule in the pilot cluster that applies different batch window and target tokens-per-bucket for each route. We'll need a 24hr run to see steady-state effects.
[02:24] Ravi (Infra): about quantization — you mentioned 8-bit earlier. Are those numbers live on the pilot or theoretical?
[02:29] Owen (SE): current pilot used fp16 baseline. We ran an ad-hoc 8-bit quantized test last week on a dev node and saw ~1.6x throughput improvement and a ~22% improvement in tokens/$ for the short-chat profile. We haven't pushed 4-bit yet; that can help more but may impact model quality.
[02:45] Jules (ML): quality is critical; we will evaluate on holdout prompts. If 8-bit is transparent we're happy, 4-bit needs eval tie-outs.
[02:53] Maya (AE): quick product question — you're currently on hosted pilot right? Any appetite for dedicated if the numbers work out?
[03:00] Samira (Head Product): potentially yes for predictable cost and isolation. But the procurement timeline is long, we want to show stable unit economics first.
[03:09] Emma (PM): also we'd need SOC2 details for dedicated deployment. Security is a gating factor.
[03:14] Maya (AE): we will share the SOC2 snapshot and private deployment checklist after this call.
[03:19] Owen (SE): back to numbers: I want to highlight caching savings. If we hit 60% prefix cache instead of 18% on long-doc, tokens/$ improves non-linearly because you're avoiding recomputation on the KV side for many tokens — we project an effective 2.1x improvement in tokens/sec/$ for that workload alone.
[03:36] Ravi (Infra): that projection assumes stable cache locality; our user prompts are somewhat varied. How sensitive is the cache to prompt paraphrasing?
[03:44] Owen (SE): it's somewhat sensitive. Prefix cache benefits when prompts share common prefixes or when there's consistent system messages. For paraphrases, we rely more on KV chunking heuristics. We can also enable approximate matching which increases hit-rate at the cost of potential stale KV entries; we'll need to test.
[03:58] Jules (ML): can you run the approximate match in a shadow mode so we can measure false positives on the evaluation set?
[04:03] Owen (SE): yes we can. We'll log hits and quality diffs.
[04:08] Emma (PM): curious about the tokens/sec/$ calc — do you include overhead like padding and RPC retries?
[04:14] Maya (AE): good q — our model currently counts billed tokens and includes a small network retry overhead estimate. We can add padding overhead per prompt type; I'll update the calc and send a CSV.
[04:23] Samira (Head Product): what's the target tokens/sec/$ for us to justify going dedicated or multi-region?
[04:29] Emma (PM): we're aiming for ~1,000 tokens/sec/$ for the mixed workload to have a predictable unit cost in our planning model.
[04:36] Owen (SE): achievable with running 8-bit quant plus improved caching and slightly more aggressive batching on doc route. The short-chat path will still be around 1,200 tokens/sec/$ on current configuration. Mixed workload drags it down because of the long-doc inefficiencies.
[04:51] Maya (AE): action: Owen re-run quantized sweep across short-chat and long-doc prompt sets, record P50/P95, tokens/sec/$, GPU utilization.
[04:59] Ravi (Infra): on infra changes, we'll flip the prefix cache policy in dev tonight and capture hit-rate. If hit-rate goes up we can mirror in pilot. Any config flags we need?
[05:07] Owen (SE): just the prefix_cache:enable=true and the approximate_match:true optional flag. Also increase batch_window_ms for doc-route to 35ms.
[05:16] Jules (ML): about the 24hr steady-state run — what QPS should we target? We want it to reflect production mix.
[05:22] Emma (PM): propose 40% short-chat, 60% long-doc by token volume; that's roughly what we expect in month 1. QPS can be low for long-doc but tokens high per request.
[05:31] Maya (AE): works. We'll codify the traffic mix and share the runner config.
[05:36] Owen (SE): one note on measurement: tokens/sec/$ is sensitive to billing granularity; ensure we compute GPU minutes properly and include any reserved overhead for auto-scaling buffer.
[05:46] Samira (Head Product): procurement will ask for a forecast with a 3-month ramp. Can you provide a scenario showing conservative vs aggressive caching assumptions?
[05:54] Maya (AE): yes, we'll provide three scenarios: conservative (18% cache hit), expected (50% cache hit), optimistic (70% hit) and show tokens/sec/$ and monthly cost at projected QPS.
[06:05] Emma (PM): what about fallback policies if load spikes or we lose dedicated nodes? Does Redwood route to cheaper model variants?
[06:12] Owen (SE): yes we have smart routing policies — canary to smaller quantized variants and fallback to cheaper region or smaller context model. We can define an A/B rollout and an automatic fallback at 85% utilization. That will affect latency during failover but keeps service up.
[06:26] Ravi (Infra): any concerns on data residency if fallback hits other regions?
[06:30] Maya (AE): we can limit routing to approved regions only. For the pilot we'll keep EU and US regions only, no APAC. We'll document that in the runbook.
[06:39] Jules (ML): can Redwood provide a one-page showing quality deltas for 8-bit and 4-bit on our holdout? That will help the execs.
[06:46] Owen (SE): yes, we'll produce a small table: BLEU/ROUGE style metrics for the summarization set and an LLM-tuned pairwise eval for chat. 8-bit usually shows near-zero delta; 4-bit needs spot checks.
[06:58] Emma (PM): for the tokens/sec/$ curve could you show both per-endpoint and blended? Blended is what finance will look at.
[07:04] Maya (AE): we'll share both.
[07:07] Samira (Head Product): anything else on risks? I want to highlight that unpredictable prompt patterns could keep cache low and that will be the main swing factor.
[07:15] Owen (SE): agreed — prompt diversity and paraphrases are the dominant sensitivity. We'll run prompt clustering to estimate reachable cache hit-rate. Jules will lead with us.
[07:23] Jules (ML): ok I can run clustering and share a short report by Monday.
[07:28] Maya (AE): logistics — we'll run the 24hr steady-state starting Monday 02:00 UTC as discussed. Owen, can you orchestrate the run and Lina capture logs?
[07:38] Owen (SE): yes. We'll include GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV hit-rate, P50/P95 and tokens/sec/$ sampled every 5 minutes.
[07:47] Lina (Solutions Eng): I'll add tracing hooks so you can correlate a particular request to KV load.
[07:52] Emma (PM): last thing — can you quantify expected monthly spend at projected 1M tokens/day under conservative vs optimistic caching?
[07:59] Maya (AE): we'll include in the one-pager. Quick back-of-envelope: at current mixed pilot numbers conservative case is ~$9k/month, expected ~$4.2k/month, optimistic ~$2.1k/month — rough numbers, we'll produce an accurate table.
[08:15] Samira (Head Product): good. let's keep momentum.
[08:19] Maya (AE): wrap up recap — Owen re-run quantized sweep and set up approximate match shadow, Ravi enable prefix cache, Jules run prompt clustering + provide holdout sets, Maya to send updated cost sheet and SOC2 snapshot. We'll reconvene after 24hr run to review steady-state. Any objections?
[08:36] Emma (PM): none. Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Maya (AE): thanks, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Notes on artifacts referenced:
- "pilot-cost-calculation.csv" (will be shared by Maya)
- "8bit-vs-fp16-benchmark-raw.csv" (Owen to upload)
- "prefix-cache-config.patch" (Ravi to apply and share diff)
- one-page exec summary PDF (Maya to draft)

Quality / transcription notes: auto-transcript had occasional speaker swaps (Maya/Owen) and some technical terms mis-recognized (KV vs Key-Vault sometimes transcribed strangely).
